links.outcome: Detection of model performance decay (calibration drift) in a frozen 2-year post-resection mortality model
links.effect: Discrimination stayed stable (optimism-corrected development AUC 0.76; later eras 0.74 and 0.75), but the calibration intercept drifted to -0.54 and -0.31 (both 95% CIs excluding zero), with over-prediction in both access strata. Predicted mortality was 19.2% against 15.6% observed, and intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large without changing discrimination.
links.quote: Discrimination-based validation can conceal clinically meaningful calibration drift.
